name: Replacing Kitchen Cabinets: What to Expect During the Renovation Process

step.name: Step 1: Planning, layout verification, and utility permits
step.text: Your contractor confirms exact wall and floor dimensions, finalizes the cabinet order, and checks with the local building department to determine whether permits are required for the project or related utility shifts. This phase sets your delivery timeline and ensures the new boxes fit your space and appliances perfectly.

step.name: Step 2: Safe disconnection of utilities and tear-out
step.text: The crew shuts off water, gas, and power to the kitchen area before disconnecting the sink, faucet, and cooking appliances. Countertops are carefully removed, followed by the demolition of old cabinet boxes and hardware. Debris is hauled away, leaving the room ready for thorough wall and floor evaluation.

step.name: Step 3: Wall repairs, framing adjustments, and rough utility work
step.text: Once the old boxes are down, the team inspects the exposed drywall, studs, and subfloor for past water leaks or uneven framing. Any needed framing repairs, drywall patching, or plumbing and electrical rough-ins take place during this step so everything behind the cabinetry is fully sound and up to standard.

step.name: Step 4: Box installation, precise leveling, and countertop templating
step.text: New cabinet boxes are mounted, leveled with shims, and secured straight into wall studs. With the base boxes firmly fastened and level, the countertop fabricator visits the home to take exact templates for your new stone or laminate counters, which then go into custom fabrication.

step.name: Step 5: Countertop setting, trim carpentry, and final hardware installation
step.text: After countertops are installed, the crew sets the cabinet doors, adjusts hinges for even gaps, inserts drawers, and mounts all decorative hardware, crown molding, and toe kicks. Sinks and appliances are reconnected and tested. Abraham Becerra and HH Remodeling LLC manage every phase of kitchen cabinet replacement with open communication and quality finish carpentry.
